prompt:
Create a high-fidelity homepage art-direction proposal for ARK Web Services, Charlotte-based web studio for service businesses nationwide. Render the website itself edge to edge at approximately1440px wide and1120px tall: legible navigation, offer, primary contact action, one huge real owned-product showcase, and the next service passage. No browser frame around the page, laptop, desk, fake staff, moodboard or external labels. A sophisticated, composed commercial website, not a poster.

This is the independent reviewer's practical-studio direction: forest #163D36, warm paper #F3EDE2, clay #BD4E2F, pale sage #D9E6DD, ink #202A26. Color fields must carry whole regions, not merely accents on a blank page. Strong distinctive humanist sans display lettering, sturdy and beautifully proportioned, clean readable body sans. Avoid the generic cream/high-contrast-serif/terracotta agency look: NO high-contrast serif, italic title, tiny uppercase eyebrow, micro-mono labels or decorative hairline grid. The actual product subject and editorial composition carry sophistication. Material is flat and tactile through color and proportion, not simulated paper grain, gradients or glass.

STRUCTURE, ONE DOMINANT MOMENT: Compact warm-paper navigation at top, ARK Web Services at left, Services / Work / Tools / About at right. Below, a short broad warm-paper title passage with a massive forest headline spanning most of the width, not an ordinary copy-left/image-right split hero. Support is quieter and short. One unmistakable clay review button sits immediately below the title before the image, comfortably visible within the first500px. Then a deep-forest exhibition field starts and contains one huge confidently cropped ACTUAL Overflow Sites interface supplied as the reference, close enough that it is visibly a designed website rather than a tiny thumbnail. The image crosses the paper/forest boundary at a measured offset and takes more than half the comp's visual area. It must feel like a major editorial work spread, not a tilted floating browser or a dashboard collage. A narrow warm-paper caption tab attaches to the showcase with accurate ownership caption and no result claims. At the bottom the pale-sage service passage begins with practical problem labels in open, uneven editorial columns, not equal cards. There is no client-logo row or testimonial strip.

EXACT CORE TEXT: wordmark 'ARK' with 'Web Services'. Navigation 'Services' 'Work' 'Tools' 'About'. Main heading 'Get your website
back on track.' Short support 'WordPress repairs, redesigns, custom development and one-time SEO foundations for service businesses.' Primary button 'Get a free site review'. Reassurance 'Written scope and project price before work begins.' Location 'Charlotte, NC · Working nationwide'. Caption on the large real interface 'Overflow Sites · related owned product'. Secondary caption 'A real interface from the ARK family of projects.' No client or performance label. Next section title 'A clear way forward.' A few visible service labels 'Fix what’s broken.' 'Rethink what’s there.' 'Build what’s missing.' Body at16–18px on1440px page, deliberate spacious hierarchy, honest and human. Avoid new pricing, timelines or lead/ranking guarantees.

REFERENCE ROLE: The supplied screenshot is the actual live Overflow Sites related owned product, used ONLY inside the major work showcase. Preserve its dark-teal/lime identity and recognizably actual headline and website interface; do not apply its lime palette or offer to ARK's surrounding homepage. Its internal browser-and-lead graphic is an illustration of its agency partnership offer, not a client result; do not invent extra metrics or label it as client proof. Surround it with forest/paper ARK design as specified. No generated fictitious portfolio, staff or customers. The existing free-review action uses an email path; do not invent a new working form. Make the first-time visitor understand the real services, see genuine work, and find one clear next action.
reference: Actual Overflow Sites live homepage, related owned product; screenshot provenance recorded separately
